MGIMS celebrates Foundation Day and Graduation Ceremony of MBBS 2020 Batch
Friday, 11 September 2026
589 Hits
On 11 September 2026, the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, celebrated its Foundation Day and the Graduation Ceremony of the MBBS 2020 Batch at the New Auditorium of the institute. Dr. Pankaj Kanchan Rajesh Bhoyar, Hon’ble State Minister, Government of Maharashtra for Home (Rural), Housing, School Education, Co-operative, Mining and Guardian Minister for Wardha, was the Chief Guest of the function. Dr BS Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr Poonam Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital) and Dr Satish Kumar (Officer In-Charge, Student Council) were present on the dais. The event was attended by faculty, staff, students, residents, press and parents of the graduates.
Addressing the graduating students, Chief Guest Dr. Pankaj Bhoyar, highlighted the profound responsibility that comes with being a doctor. Referring to the MBBS 2020 Batch as “Corona Warriors,” he said, “When you entered medical college in 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic entered our lives. Your medical education was disrupted. You saw medicine beyond textbooks. You saw what it means when a doctor stands between illness and a frightened family. You saw doctors working despite uncertainty, exhaustion and fear. And perhaps without realising it, you began learning the most important subject in medicine—humanity.” Dr. Bhoyar also lauded the institute’s efforts in providing healthcare to Wardha and the surrounding areas, particularly its commitment to the tribal population of Dharni.
Dr Pankaj Bhoyar distributed the graduation certificates and awards to the MBBS 2020 Batch. Awards were also presented to meritorious undergraduate and postgraduate students in recognition of their academic excellence and extracurricular achievements. Hospital staff and community health workers were also honoured for their dedicated service to the institution. Dr. CM Badole (Head of Orthopaedics, MGIMS) administered the Physician’s Oath to the graduating students, reaffirming their commitment to the ethical practice of medicine and service to humanity.
Shri Prataprao Ganpatrao Jadhav, Hon’ble Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Minister of State (Independent Charge) for AYUSH, Government of India, virtually graced the occasion. His message was read out by Dr. Kanchan Mohod, Professor of Biochemistry, MGIMS. In his message, Shri Jadhav said, “Your medical knowledge is not merely for a career; it is a responsibility to save lives, support families and take quality healthcare to the last person. Carry forward the legacy of Sevagram with sensitivity, empathy, humility and a spirit of service”
Shri PL Tapadiya, President, Kasturba Health Society, also virtually congratulated the graduates and extended his best wishes. Reading his message, Dr. Poonam Shivkumar said on behalf of Shri P. L. Tapadiya, “You shall always remain the ambassadors of MGIMS. Wherever life takes you, carry with you the values that Sevagram has sought to nurture in you.” Dr. A. K. Shukla, Dean, MGIMS, highlighted the significance of the occasion for the graduating batch and the institution. Dr BS Garg, “You are doctor trained at one of India's finest institutions. Mgims doctors is a five star doctor. Whenever you are unsure about what is right, look towards the person who needs you the most.
Sharing his reflections upon graduating, Dr Prafulla Dhere from the MGIMS Batch of 2020 said, “As we look back, we realise that our journey at MGIMS was about much more than becoming doctors—it was about the friendships, the memories and the countless moments that shaped us. We leave Sevagram today with a deep sense of gratitude and nostalgia, carrying a little piece of MGIMS with us wherever we go”.
Dr Anshu (Professor of Pathology) and Dr Abhay Deshmukh (Associate Professor of Pathology) compered the programme. The ceremony concluded with the Vote of Thanks, followed by the National Anthem
